notes.title: DEEPWATER Demo Beta out NOW!
notes.content:
Hello! The netcode beta is finally out. I'll explain some more of what that means in a bit, but for now, lets talk about whats coming.

Oh, in case you don't know how to access the beta, here is how:
Right click the DEEPWATER Demo in your steam library, click Properties, find the betas tab, and opt into the netcode-beta branch. Wait for the game to update, and enjoy.

Alright, whats this for? Well, this beta is meant to help me find every single issue with the new version. Sure, I could keep it private and slowly find issues and fix them, or I could involve you guys to speed things up. I would rather speed things up, and I think you guys would like things to move along faster too.

The beta is starting small, with less content then the main version. When I know everything works properly, I re-add content. Once I'm sure that the content works properly, I re-add even more. 
We do this until the game is back to normal. 

Whats coming once this is done? Well, I promised a major content update for the demo, and a major update is what your gonna get. I've been planning an update for multiple months now, and I wont say much, but this will change everything. Each major update will be like this by the way, I'm not gonna slow down and barely add anything and pass it off as an update. Each major update will be game changing.

After that content update comes out, I'll give it some time, and then release the game as a paid product.
The demo will probably close once the game goes live, but if enough people really want it, I will create a special demo version of the game to stay forever.

Alright, enough yapping about the future, whats all this netcode stuff I keep talking about? Well, the netcode is what makes the game multiplayer. Each multiplayer service provider provides netcode for me to use to make my game multiplayer. The old service I used was pretty bad. I only used it because it was what I was familiar with. I've made many tiny multiplayer games with their service, and they've been great. Keyword TINY. DEEPWATER is not a tiny game. 

DEEPWATER just had so much going on that it couldn't keep up, and that caused tons and tons of bugs. It didn't help that all of the servers were located in the US, so if you were far away, you automatically were going to have a bad time. From horrible lag, to some things not showing up for some players, it was horrible. I wasn't able to catch these bugs during development, since me and most of my playtesters are close to the US.

So I had 2 options. Stay on the old system and continue with what I am comfortable with, and turn many people off from the game, or switch to a completely new system. 
I chose to switch.

This involved completely rewriting all of the games netcode, and changing how many game systems work. As you can imagine, this isn't a one-and-done thing, bugs will slip through. That's why I'm doing the beta.

Alright, enough from me, thank you to anyone who tries the beta, and reports bugs to me. If you don't know how to report bugs, you can join my Discord server, and I have a dedicated channel for bug reporting. Also happy new year.

notes.title: DEEPWATER's First Major Content Update is Coming Soon
notes.content:
Hello! Its been a minute since I last updated the game. Things didn't go as expected, and I was forced to switch multiplayer services. 

As you can imagine, this is a monumental task, especially for someone who is working alone (me).
Don't worry though, it's almost done! Right now, the new build is not accessible, due to some things still not working properly. I'm hard at work getting this ready for you all to try!

This has been something that honestly, was inevitable. The old service was easy to use, but limited. 
It's what was causing most of the issues, from items getting desynced, to things not even showing for some people. This new service is much more complex, but much more stable and secure.

Once it's ready, there will be a public beta you can try that will be using the new multiplayer service. I hope to have this beta out by the end of the month. 

[b]For now, the beta will only let you join people through Steam invites.[/b]

Once the beta is out and all the remaining issues have been dealt with, its new content time! 
I've been planning a major content update for the demo, focusing on guns. I've wanted this game to be focused on guns ever since the start, but right now in their current state most players either don't know they exist, can't get them, or simply don't think they are useful enough. 

The update isn't just going to be "[i]I updated the guns to be better goodbye[/i]".
I don't want to spoil too much, but the new content is going to change the entire game.
I want every single major content update I make to be game changing, and offer new ways to play. 
[b]They wont just be 1 or 2 new creatures and a new item.[/b]

Also, the voice chat is gonna sound a lot different. It's a long story, but you know that popping/buzzing sound bug? That was due to how I was getting the voice chat to have all of the audio effects of the audio engine, since I don't use the built in audio engine (BIG MISTAKE). 

Since I had to switch multiplayer services, I also had to switch voice chat providers. 
I'm not going to bother getting the voice chat to have the audio effects, since it sucks.

Soon after this is all over, I will be migrating away from the current audio engine over to the built in one. This will also be a long and painful process, but it will be worth it.

Oh, and the lantern item is getting removed. It's funny watching people buy it, and immediately kill themselves with it. Funny, but unfair and confusing. Doesn't belong in a game about skill and teamwork.

Alright, that's enough rambling from me. Thank you everyone who has tried the game and given me feedback, it means the world to me. 

As always, if you want to leave bug reports, or feedback, or just say hi, you can join my Discord server.
